properties.chose:
Anthony, 2026-10-01: "I tried to talk to my boss about how the github subscription works, but he wouldn't listen and said it was very hard to change to allow for reflow2 mcp, so it sounds like we'll have to make the '--call' option work as best we can."
(10) THE ALLOWLIST was asked about and is not available in his organisation. Changing the Copilot subscription's MCP policy was judged "very hard". GitHub's "MCP servers in Copilot" policy and its "Registry only" allowlist remain the clean route wherever an admin will use them.
(c) THE `--call` DOOR is the route.
(9) A VS CODE EXTENSION registering reflow2's tools is not pursued now.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's ideas 9 and 10 in using_call.md (2026-10-01), and the policy question the document raises for idea 9 only.

THE IDEAS, in his words:
(10) "Ask the admin about an MCP registry allowlist. If the org policy is registry-based rather than off entirely, adding reflow2 to the allowed registry restores the normal setup, and every limitation above goes away."
(9) "A VS Code extension that registers Language Model Tools" (`vscode.lm.registerTool`): each served tool becomes a first-class Copilot tool with its schema, backed by `--call` or a long-lived local process. That fixes limitations 3, 4 and 8. His own caution: "Check with IT first: if the policy's intent is 'no unvetted agent tools' rather than 'no MCP transport', an extension that reintroduces the tools is the wrong answer."
(c) The `--call` door as it stands (dec:idea-the-call-door-becomes-a-supported-harness-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp).

A FINDING FROM THE REVIEW, NOT A VERDICT: his caution on (9) applies equally to (c). The door gives the same agent the same tools through the terminal. Whether that is within the policy turns on its intent, and only the admin can say. So (10) answers the question every other option depends on, and it costs one conversation.

THE RULE: rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground. (10) restores its one assumption, while (9) and (c) are additions for one product, which the rule permits but never as the mechanism.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-01 — where an org blocks third-party MCP and will not allowlist reflow2, the `--call` door is the route, made to work as well as it can
